RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the August 2, 2005/Sravana 11, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Finance; Panchayati Raj;
Petroleum and Natural Gas; Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions —20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Utilisation of Rupsi Airport
*121. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to utilise the Rupsi Airport near
Dhubari in Assam;
(b) if so, what steps have been taken by
Government till now; and
(c) whether there is any commitment
from Government to the NER MPs in this
regard?
Offer of cheap air tickets by private
airlines
†*122. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
certain private airlines have tried to dupe
ordinary passengers by offering to sell air
ticket for Re. 1/-;
(b) whether some companies also offer
air travel for Rs. 222/- in the name of
competition;
(c) whether Government propose to set
up a regulatory authority to regulate the
travel fare of all airlines in order to protect
the ordinary passengers from market
competition of private companies;
(d) whether Government propose to
take any action against the private airlines
duping passengers by offering cheap
tickets; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Investment of pension funds in capital
market
*123. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal for
investment of pension fund of Central
Government employees in the capital
market;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the present status of the above proposal;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
allow Foreign Direct Investment and
Private Fund Managers in the pension fund
of Central Government employees; and

38
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(d) if so, the details and the present
status of above proposal?
Policy on parking space at airports
*124. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRI JANARDAN
DWIVEDI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that parking space
at airport terminals reserved for
Government airlines is now being given to
private airlines for their use;
(b) whether it is also a fact that some of
the private airlines have been given parking
rights by dereserving Government airlines
space and no policy or rule were followed
in doing so; and
(c) the policy/rules for providing
parking space to different airlines at metro
airports?
Diplomacy on oil
*125. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether India is all set to launch
another round of oil diplomacy in mid-
October;
(b) whether in its attempt to form an
Asian Oil Community, India will host
another meeting of Central Asian Oil
producers with the four largest consumers
of Asia viz. China, Korea, Japan and India;
(c) whether India proposes to host a
meeting of Oil Ministers from Russia,
Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan
and Azerbaijan with four prime Asian
buyers;
(d) if so, what will be the main points
of discussion with Oil Ministers;
(e) the details thereof; and
(f) what are steps proposed to be taken
to have a fresh diplomacy on oil?
Shortage of runways at Delhi airport
*126. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that planes have
to wait for an hour to take-off from Delhi
airport due to lack of space, etc.;
(b) whether Government have any plan
to meet the shortage of runway space in
the immediate future;
(c) to what extent the AAI has been
able to meet the anticipated growth in air
traffic in Delhi;
(d) what immediate steps will be taken
to find ways to meet the demand of space
for landings and take-offs at Delhi;
(e) whether a more scientific use can be
made of existing runways; and
(f) the steps proposed to meet this
challenge immediately?
Foreign institutions in Indian share
market
†*127. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the number
of foreign institutions is increasing rapidly
in the share market of the country;

39
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that
the number of foreign companies was 68 in
March, 2005 which has increased to 721
till 10th June, 2005;
(c) if so, the details in this regard; and
(d) the reasons for foreign financial
institutions entering rapidly in the Indian
share market?
Impact of prices of crude oil on the
inflation rate

SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the inflation
rate has been more in the financial year
2004-05 in comparison to the last five years;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;

List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS

————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Finance; Panchayati Raj;
Petroleum and Natural Gas; Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 155
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Flights handled at major airports
799. SHRI ANAND SHARMA: Will
the Minister  of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the international and
domestic flights currently being handled at
Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai and
Kolkata airports;
(b) the projected increase in the flights
at these airports in the next three years;
and
(c) the steps proposed for upgradation
of the major airports for flight and
passenger handling?
Expansion of runway at Patna
airport
800. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL:Will the Minister  of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that length of the
runway of Patna airport is less in
comparison to the runways of other national
level airports; and
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government
for the expansion thereof, so far?
Old aircrafts with AI
801. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister  of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) when the last time Air India ordered
new planes for its fleet;
(b) the details of new planes bought by
Air India in the last three years;
(c) to what extent Air India is using
planes which exceed 15 years age;
(d) whether it is a fact that safety and
speed are ignored by Air India; and
(e) the steps proposed to upgrade the
fleet of Air India?
Decline in IA's market share
802. SHRI C. PERUMAL:
SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY:
Will the Minister  of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the market
share of Indian Airlines has come down to
38.2 per cent when compared to the
previous market share of 65.9 per cent in

184
1997-98 due to competition by the private
sector in aviation industry; and
(b) if so, what measures Government
are taking to improve its market share in
the coming years?
Operation of  international services
by AI
803. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister  of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the global
civil aviation market and the tourist sector
are poised to grow annually by 20 per
cent;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the Air
India had taken a decision to operate
international flights from cities other than
Delhi and Mumbai;
(c) whether it is also a fact that Air India
had chalked out ambitious plans to
overcome shortage of planes; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Liquidation of companies
804. SHRI MURLI DEORA: Will the
Minister  of COMPANY AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Governemnt propose to
quicken the process of liquidations of
companies to protect the interests of stake
holders;
(b) if so, the details of, the norms framed
in this regard;
(c) the number of firms which are under
liquidation; and
(d) the average time taken to complete
the proceedings for such liquidation?
Development of support systems for
air safety
805. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister  of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
movement of both the domestic and
international aircrafts has tremendously
increased during the last two years
whereas development of support systems
crucial for air safety has received little
attention from Government;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons for not attending to support
systems; and
(c) what action Government propose
to take in that direction?
Parking space at airports
806. SHRI JANARDAN
DWIVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister  of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that airports in
metro cities are jostling for the space of
aircraft parking;
(b)  the no. of aircrafts which could be
parked at the airports of Delhi, Mumbai,
Kolkata, Chennai, Bangalore and
Hyderabad; and
(c) the no. of applications which are
pending with the Airports Authority of
India in this regard?

185
Pilot training institutes
†807. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL:
SHRI C. PERUMAL:
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
Will the Minister  of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is acute
shortage of pilot training institutes in the
country;
(b) whether it is also a fact that due to
the above shortage, there has been acute
shortage of trained pilots (Aeroplane and
Helicopter) in the country;
(c) if so, the details of efforts being made
by Government in this regard;
(d) the details of Government and
recognised institutes operating all over the
country;
(e) whether any proposal regarding
opening of the above institute in Madhya
Pradesh is pending with Government; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Evening air service between Delhi and
Guwahati

(a) whether Government propose to
introduce evening flight f
